extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and registered patent practitioners (U.S. patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on specifying, changing, and correcting the correspondence address and on preparing and updating the Application Data Sheet (ADS) in U.S. patent applications, including who may change addresses, required ADS headings, and rules for corrected ADS submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address requirement (37 CFR 1.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must specify a correspondence address in either an application data sheet (§ 1.76) or elsewhere in a clearly identifiable manner in any paper submitted with the application filing; if none is specified, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first-named inventor as the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will direct notices, official letters, and other communications to the person associated with the correspondence address. For correspondence submitted via EFS-Web, an electronic acknowledgement will be sent to the submitter. The Office generally will not engage in double correspondence except as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection when more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document, the Office will select one of the specified addresses for use as the correspondence address and will select the address associated with a Customer Number over a typed correspondence address if given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a single clear correspondence designation or use a Customer Number to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority among conflicting correspondence addresses across documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant directs the Office to use non-matching correspondence addresses in more than one paper, priority will be accorded in this order: (A) Application Data Sheet (ADS); (B) Application transmittal; (C) Oath or declaration (unless power of attorney is more current); and (D) Power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office treats the ADS as the most recently created and likely most current document; ensure the ADS contains the intended correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daytime telephone number
rubrics_metrics.description: For the party to whom correspondence is to be addressed, a daytime telephone number should be supplied in a clearly identifiable manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A daytime telephone number is requested to facilitate initiating contact that could later be reduced to writing. Any party who may change the correspondence address may also change the telephone number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change correspondence address prior to filing oath/declaration (pre-AIA § 1.33(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a § 1.63 oath or declaration has not been filed by any of the inventors, the correspondence address may be changed by the party who filed the application; if filed by a patent practitioner, any other patent practitioner named in the transmittal papers may also change the correspondence address. An assignee who filed the application may also change it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner named only in a letterhead is not considered named in the transmittal papers for this purpose; clear identification as a representative is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change correspondence address after filing oath/declaration (pre-AIA § 1.33(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an executed § 1.63 oath or declaration has been filed by any of the inventors, the correspondence address may be changed by: (A) a patent practitioner of record, (B) an assignee as provided under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.71(b), or (C) all of the applicants under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.41(b), except where an assignee of the entire interest has taken action in accordance with 3.71.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once an executed oath/declaration is filed, the set of parties authorized to change the correspondence address narrows to those listed above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner change after patent issues (37 CFR 1.33(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner acting in a representative capacity whose correspondence address is of record in an application may change the correspondence address after the patent has issued, provided the change is accompanied by a statement that notice has been given to the patentee or owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.33(g) allows such a post-issue change but does not authorize a practitioner acting under 37 CFR 1.34 to change the correspondence address in an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuations/divisionals — ensure address changes are reflected
rubrics_metrics.description: Special care must be taken in continuation or divisional applications: if application papers (e.g., an oath or declaration) from a prior application are used and the correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, an ADS or separate paper identifying the correspondence address to be used for the continuing application must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not submitted, the Office may not recognize the change and correspondence may be mailed to the previously designated address. Applicant is required to identify the change in the continuation/divisional to ensure communications are mailed to the current correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS must comply with 37 CFR 1.76 and become part of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: An Application Data Sheet (ADS) must comply with 37 CFR 1.76, be titled 'Application Data Sheet,' contain required section headings, and when provided becomes part of the application and must comply with 37 CFR 1.52.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not always required, the Office prefers ADS use to facilitate electronic capture of data. When required (e.g., to claim priority/benefit), an ADS must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS bibliographic headings — inventor information (1.76(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor information must include the legal name, residence, and mailing address of the inventor or each joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will continue to use inventor names for identification; 'mailing address' is where the inventor customarily receives mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS bibliographic headings — correspondence information (1.76(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence information must include the correspondence address, which may be indicated by reference to a customer number, to which correspondence is to be directed (see § 1.33(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including a Customer Number helps the Office select the intended address and supports electronic processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS bibliographic headings — application information (1.76(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Application information includes the title of the invention, total number of drawing sheets, a suggested drawing figure for publication (in a nonprovisional), any docket number, the type of application (utility, plant, design, reissue, provisional), secrecy-order disclosures, and for plant applications the Latin name and variety denomination. When required under § 1.57(a), it also includes references to previously filed applications (application number, filing date, and intellectual property authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants filing by reference under 35 U.S.C. 111(c) and 37 CFR 1.57 must ensure the previously filed application's number, filing date, and authority are accurately specified on the ADS. Note the Office is not bound to print the suggested figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS bibliographic headings — representative information (1.76(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative information includes the registration number of each practitioner having a power of attorney in the application (preferably by reference to a customer number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing representative information in the ADS does not itself constitute a power of attorney in the application (see § 1.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS bibliographic headings — domestic benefit information (1.76(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic benefit information includes the application number, filing date, status (including patent number if available), and relationship of each application for which a benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 and § 1.78; continuity data for the patent front page will be taken from the ADS. This does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS bibliographic headings — foreign priority information (1.76(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority information includes the application number, country (or intellectual property authority), and filing date of each foreign application for which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the claim for priority required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and 37 CFR 1.55. This does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS bibliographic headings — applicant information (1.76(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant information includes the name (natural person or juristic entity) and address of the legal representative, assignee, person to whom the inventor is under an obligation to assign, or person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter who is the applicant under §§ 1.43 or 1.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignment information in the ADS does not substitute for compliance with requirements of part 3 to have an assignment recorded with the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting and updating an ADS (37 CFR 1.76(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information in a previously submitted ADS or information otherwise of record may be corrected or updated until payment of the issue fee by filing a new ADS providing corrected or updated information; a corrected ADS must identify the information being changed with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for text removed (except as noted for 35 U.S.C. 371 initial submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected ADS may include only the sections containing changed information and must include the section headings for each included section. Use of the corrected Web-based ADS is recommended where appropriate because it will pre-populate with information of record and generate proper strike-through/underlining. Corrected Web-based ADS is not permitted in certain application types (see separate metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency and governing-information rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For inconsistencies between an ADS and other documents, the most recent submission will govern overall, but the most recent ADS governs foreign priority (§ 1.55) and domestic benefit (§ 1.78) claims; naming of inventorship is governed by § 1.41 and changes by § 1.48. The information in the ADS will govern when inconsistent with information supplied at the same time by a designation of correspondence address or an inventor's oath or declaration, and will govern when inconsistent with certain international forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will capture bibliographic information from the ADS and generally will not review the inventor's oath/declaration for consistency with an ADS; incorrect bibliographic information in an ADS may be corrected per § 1.76(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for ADS (37 CFR 1.76(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An ADS must be signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unsigned ADS will be treated only as a transmittal letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected Web-based ADS availability and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office provides fillable ADS forms (PTO/AIA/14 and PTO/SB/14) and an enhanced Web-based ADS; a corrected Web-based ADS is available for certain existing applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 and will be pre-populated with information of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corrected Web-based ADS is not permitted in international applications, national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, provisional applications, plant applications, reexamination proceedings, and supplemental examinations under 35 U.S.C. 257. The Web ADS should be submitted as an EFS-Web fillable form (not a scanned PDF) to load directly into Office systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference filing via ADS under 37 CFR 1.57 and 35 U.S.C. 111(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Dec 18, 2013, a reference to a previously filed application made in the English language in an ADS in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76 upon filing of an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) indicating that the specification and any drawings are replaced by the reference to the previously filed application shall constitute the specification and drawings of the application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) for purposes of a filing date under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants using reference filing must still provide priority and/or benefit information under the domestic benefit or foreign priority headings in the ADS; ensure the previously filed application's number, filing date, and intellectual property authority are accurately specified on the ADS.
